title: Coding Interview Bank
note: Problems are practice material; exact questions vary by employer.

questions.prompt: Given an array and target, return indices of two values that sum to target.
questions.approach: Use a Dictionary<int,int> while scanning once.
questions.followup: Follow-up: what if input is sorted?

questions.prompt: Determine whether brackets are correctly nested.
questions.approach: Use a Stack<char> and match each closing bracket to the latest opener.
questions.followup: Follow-up: how would you handle other bracket types?

questions.prompt: Reverse a singly linked list.
questions.approach: Maintain previous, current and next pointers and reverse links iteratively.
questions.followup: Follow-up: recursive version?

questions.prompt: Return the first character that occurs once.
questions.approach: Count characters, then scan the string again.
questions.followup: Follow-up: case sensitivity?

questions.prompt: Find the longest substring with unique characters.
questions.approach: Use a sliding window and a map of last seen positions.
questions.followup: Follow-up: explain why the left boundary never moves backward.

questions.prompt: Find the contiguous subarray with maximum sum.
questions.approach: Kadane's algorithm tracks the best subarray ending at the current position.
questions.followup: Follow-up: return the actual range too.

questions.prompt: Merge overlapping intervals.
questions.approach: Sort by start, then extend the last output interval when overlap exists.
questions.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
questions.followup: Follow-up: can you process already sorted input in O(n)?

questions.prompt: Find the first position of a target in sorted data.
questions.approach: Binary search while continuing left after a match.
questions.followup: Follow-up: find the last occurrence.

questions.prompt: Return the k most frequent values.
questions.approach: Count frequencies, then use a heap or bucket strategy.
questions.complexity: O(n log k) with a heap
questions.followup: Follow-up: when is bucket sort better?

questions.prompt: Implement get and put with O(1) average operations.
questions.approach: Combine Dictionary<TKey,Node> with a doubly linked list for recency order.
questions.followup: Follow-up: make it thread-safe.

questions.prompt: Implement a bounded producer-consumer queue.
questions.approach: Use a concurrent queue plus synchronization/semaphores or a channel abstraction.
questions.followup: Follow-up: graceful shutdown?

questions.prompt: Implement retry with exponential backoff.
questions.approach: Retry only classified transient failures, cap attempts and delay, and honor cancellation.
questions.followup: Follow-up: why add jitter?

questions.prompt: Count connected land components in a grid.
questions.approach: DFS/BFS each unvisited land cell and mark the component.
questions.followup: Follow-up: iterative BFS to avoid recursion depth.

questions.prompt: Determine whether prerequisites contain a cycle.
questions.approach: Model a directed graph and use Kahn's algorithm or DFS cycle detection.
questions.followup: Follow-up: return a valid ordering.

questions.prompt: Determine whether a string can be segmented using dictionary words.
questions.approach: Use dynamic programming where dp[i] indicates whether prefix i is constructible.
questions.followup: Follow-up: how would a trie change it?

questions.prompt: Find minimum rooms required for overlapping meetings.
questions.approach: Sort starts and ends or use a min-heap of end times.
questions.followup: Follow-up: return which room each meeting uses.

questions.prompt: Build an expiring cache safe for concurrent readers/writers.
questions.approach: Define key/value/expiry semantics, use concurrent structures and avoid duplicate expensive factories.
questions.complexity: Correctness and bounded memory matter more than raw speed.
questions.followup: Follow-up: cache stampede and eviction strategy?

questions.prompt: Implement a per-client rate limiter.
questions.approach: Use token bucket or sliding window semantics with atomic state and expiration.
questions.followup: Follow-up: how would multiple API instances share limits?

questions.prompt: Build a worker that accepts jobs, limits concurrency and shuts down gracefully.
questions.approach: Use a bounded queue, cancellation token, worker loop and completion signaling.
questions.followup: Follow-up: what happens to jobs during shutdown?

questions.prompt: Process many files concurrently without exhausting memory.
questions.approach: Stream files, bound concurrency, use cancellation, collect failures and make processing idempotent.
questions.complexity: Complexity depends on total bytes; memory remains bounded.
questions.followup: Follow-up: resume after process failure.
